output.question: What are the details of Bayer's merger with Monsanto?
output.answer: Bayer agreed on September 14, 2016 to acquire Monsanto through a Bayer subsidiary merging into Monsanto, with Monsanto surviving as a wholly owned Bayer subsidiary; the agreed consideration was $128.00 in cash per Monsanto share. [https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1110783/000119312516714915/d234658dex21.htm](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1110783/000119312516714915/d234658dex21.htm) Bayer completed the transaction on June 7, 2018, became Monsanto's sole owner, and Monsanto shares ceased trading; Bayer described the total cost as approximately $63 billion including Monsanto's debt. [https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/bayer-closes-monsanto-acquisition/](https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/bayer-closes-monsanto-acquisition/) [https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/bayer-plans-closing-of-monsanto-acquisition-on-june-7/](https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/bayer-plans-closing-of-monsanto-acquisition-on-june-7/) Regulatory clearance required divestitures to BASF: businesses generating €2.2 billion in 2017 sales for a €7.6 billion base price, while the U.S. Justice Department described the required package as approximately $9 billion to address horizontal and vertical competition concerns. [https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/bayer-plans-closing-of-monsanto-acquisition-on-june-7/](https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/bayer-plans-closing-of-monsanto-acquisition-on-june-7/) [https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-secures-largest-merger-divestiture-ever-preserve-competition-threatened](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/justice-department-secures-largest-merger-divestiture-ever-preserve-competition-threatened) Bayer said the combination would double the size of its agriculture business; Bayer remained the company name, Monsanto did not, and acquired products retained their brands. [https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/bayer-plans-closing-of-monsanto-acquisition-on-june-7/](https://www.bayer.com/media/en-us/bayer-plans-closing-of-monsanto-acquisition-on-june-7/)

key_facts.fact: The September 14, 2016 merger agreement provided for KWA Investment Co., an indirect wholly owned Bayer subsidiary, to merge into Monsanto; Monsanto would survive and become a wholly owned Bayer subsidiary.
The merger consideration was $128.00 per Monsanto share in cash, without interest.
Bayer completed the acquisition on June 7, 2018; Bayer became Monsanto's sole owner and Monsanto shares were no longer traded on the New York Stock Exchange.
Bayer stated that the transaction's approximate total cost was $63 billion including Monsanto's debt outstanding as of February 28, 2018.
For regulatory approval, Bayer agreed to divest businesses that generated €2.2 billion in 2017 sales for an aggregate base purchase price of €7.6 billion; the divestitures were to BASF.

The U.S. Department of Justice said Bayer had to divest businesses and assets worth approximately $9 billion to resolve horizontal and vertical competition concerns; the package included Bayer cotton, canola, soybean and vegetable seed businesses, Liberty herbicide, certain seed-treatment businesses, intellectual property, R&D and digital-agriculture assets.

Bayer said the combination would double the size of its agriculture business; Bayer would remain the company name, Monsanto would no longer be a company name, and acquired products would retain their brand names.

passages.quote: This AGREEMENT AND PLAN OF MERGER (this “Agreement”), dated as of September 14, 2016, is by and among Bayer Aktiengesellschaft, a German stock corporation (“Parent”), KWA Investment Co., a Delaware corporation and an indirect wholly-owned Subsidiary of Parent (“Merger Sub”), and Monsanto Company
Merger Sub shall be merged with and into the Company ... The Company shall be the surviving corporation in the Merger ... and, following the Merger, shall be a wholly-owned Subsidiary of Parent
Each Share ... shall be converted into the right to receive $128.00 ... per Share in cash, without interest

Bayer successfully completed the acquisition of Monsanto on Thursday. Shares in the U.S. company will no longer be traded on the New York Stock Exchange, with Bayer now the sole owner of Monsanto Company.

Bayer announced its intention to acquire Monsanto in May 2016 and signed an agreement with the U.S. company for 128 U.S. dollars per share in September 2016. Currently that corresponds to a total cost of approximately 63 billion U.S. dollars taking into account Monsanto’s debt outstanding as of February 28, 2018.
Bayer ... agreed to the divestiture of businesses which generated 2.2 billion euros in sales in 2017 for an aggregate base purchase price of 7.6 billion euros.

The Department of Justice announced today that it is requiring Bayer AG to divest businesses and assets collectively worth approximately $9 billion in order to proceed with its proposed $66 billion acquisition of Monsanto Company.

caveats: The headline transaction value varies by definition: Bayer cited approximately $63 billion including Monsanto debt as of February 28, 2018, while the DOJ described the proposed acquisition as $66 billion and the divestiture package as approximately $9 billion.
The DOJ page is archived and was updated February 5, 2025; the transaction itself closed in 2018.
Bayer's stated expected synergies and earnings effects were forward-looking projections at the time, not verified outcomes, so they are not included as realized results.

input: What are the details of Bayer's merger with Monsanto?
